pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.

6. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

7. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

9. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.

11. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

14. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. watt (W)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
15. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

2. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

4. B — Glucose and oxygen

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.

6. A — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

7. A — Producers

8. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

11. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.

13. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

14. B — newton (N)
